laws.rule: Waterford City and County Council Beach Bye-Laws 2021 apply year round to the scheduled beaches and strands in the council area, including Strand Beach and the pier at Tramore, Newtown Cove and Guillameen, Clonea, Ardmore, Bunmahon, Annestown, Woodstown, Passage Strand, and the Dunmore East strands (Counsellors Strand, Main Strand, Ladies Cove and others listed in the First Schedule). On those beaches it is forbidden to light an open fire (other than in a contained unit such as a barbecue), damage dunes or plants, remove sand, stones, seaweed or soil without consent, set off fireworks, camp or erect a tent or caravan, drive or park a motor vehicle, camper, quad bike or similar on the beach or dunes, stay overnight in a campervan, motor home or motor caravan between 11:00 pm and 06:00 am, sell or hire goods or offer tuition without a council licence, or film on a commercial basis without consent. Personal watercraft may be launched only from an existing slipway, not from beaches, must keep to 5 knots for 300 metres seaward when launching, and must not be used within 300 metres of the low water mark except for rescue or access at a slipway; a suitable personal flotation device must be worn. Horses may be brought onto the beach in the summer season (1 May to 30 September) only between 5:00 am and 11:00 am, and not onto the dunes except for access. Fishing is not allowed in the bathing areas at Guillameen and Newtown Cove. An authorised person or a member of An Garda Síochána can exclude or remove someone who breaches the bye-laws, demand their name, address and photographic identification, and issue an on-the-spot fixed payment of EUR 75 (about A$119 at RBA 30 Oct 2026, A$1 = EUR 0.6293). A person who contravenes the bye-laws is also liable on summary conviction to a fine not exceeding EUR 1,904.60 (about A$3,027), and EUR 126.97 (about A$202) for each day a contravention continues after conviction.

items.text: On the beaches and strands listed in the Waterford City and County Council Beach Bye-Laws 2021, no person may consume alcohol, or organise an event which involves consumption of alcohol, except with the consent of the Council and subject to the terms of that consent. The bye-laws apply year round. A simple breach can be dealt with by an on-the-spot fixed payment of EUR 75 (about A$119 at RBA 30 Oct 2026, A$1 = EUR 0.6293), or a fine not exceeding EUR 1,904.60 (about A$3,027) on summary conviction.
